design.question: [scripted] Does the simulated fly's time-to-contact avoidance rule reduce collisions in pillar clutter?
design.hypothesis: [scripted] Saccading away from surfaces under 0.45 s to contact reduces collision episodes per metre flown.
design.competing_hypothesis: [scripted] Spontaneous saccades and the arena layout alone set the collision rate; the avoidance rule changes little.

ir.question: In the digital fly simulator, how does turning away from surfaces whose time to contact falls below 0.45 s change collision episodes that began in cruising flight (not during a landing approach) per metre flown in pillar clutter, against avoidance off (avoidTtcS = 0) on matched seeds?
ir.hypothesis: Turning away from surfaces whose time to contact falls below 0.45 s will decrease cruise_collision_episodes_per_m by at least 0.1 1/m on average over matched seeds, compared with avoidance off (avoidTtcS = 0), in the expected direction in at least 8 of 12 seeds.

observables.description: collision episodes per metre flown in pillar clutter
collision episodes that began in cruising flight (not during a landing approach) per metre flown in pillar clutter
collision episodes in pillar clutter (contacts less than 0.1 s apart are one episode)
body saccades per second of flight in pillar clutter
time spent pressed against a surface while flying or landing in pillar clutter
treatment minus control cruise_collision_episodes_per_m, averaged over seeds

independent_variables: turning away from surfaces whose time to contact falls below 0.45 s
controls: matched seeds: each seed places the fly, draws its stimuli and seeds its random streams identically in both arms
fixed apparatus settings, both arms — clutter block: takeoffHz = 0.5
the fly's version, controller and full parameter table are bound into the plan digest
parameter_constraints: six closed protocols with host-built arenas and stimuli
controller configurations override model parameters only; FlyBody and published values are fixed
the integration settings (physics, sensing and decision periods) are never varied
at most 16000 simulated fly-seconds per experiment
8-16 distinct seeds; the effect must appear in at least half of them

statistical_analysis.method: Matched-seed paired difference of the primary metric; per-seed sign counts; frozen rain-criteria/v1
statistical_analysis.uncertainty: Seeds are independent replicates of one reduced-order model; descriptive only, with no p-value or population inference, and nothing about real flies.

limitations: The digital fly's controller is a reduced-order state machine. It simulates no neurons; its links to Virtual Fly Brain terms are labels, not mechanisms.
Model parameters were chosen for this simulator, not measured or fitted; a result describes the simulator with these values.
Flight is kinematic: no aerodynamics and no MuJoCo physics run in these experiments.
The arena is a box with primitive obstacles and a relative light proxy (not lux); odour, temperature, humidity, airflow and food are not simulated.
A result characterizes the simulator and is never empirical evidence about Drosophila.

guards.note: An independent re-simulation reproduces every state hash and measurement

failure.note: No effect or the opposite direction
